why: The board calls Leach a highly effective legislator with a moral core; it says it is skeptical the state can raise enough money to replace local school property taxes, as he proposes.
The board cites Plesa's record of turning ideas into law and building coalitions with Republicans; it calls Flint's legal and judicial experience strong qualifications.

The board respects Hill's record for residents worried about property taxes but worries his pointedly partisan style can't unite a changing county; it found Brown personable but short on experience for the office.
The board urges a yes on all four county bonds; it notes Prop A's $296.5 million for courtrooms and 550 more jail beds, and says the county can afford these bonds.
The board urges a yes on all four county bonds; it notes Prop B's $475 million for roads, including Dallas North Tollway service roads and the Outer Loop, and says the county can afford these bonds.
The board urges a yes on all four county bonds; Prop C, the smallest, is $6 million for parks and open space.
The board urges a yes on all four county bonds; it notes Prop D's $40 million building for elections and records would replace space the county leases for about $650,000 a year.
